From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@mediqhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@mediqhealth.com

Subject: Request: Custom SLO rider + onboarding checklist (MSA & Order Form sign-off)

Diego,

Thanks for taking this on — Mediq Health is preparing to finalize our MSA and the associated Order Form but procurement has flagged a need for a bespoke SLO/rider for availability and latency guarantees tied to our Dedicated capacity commitment. High level asks: 

- Target availability: 99.95% monthly for API endpoints used by our care workflows
- Latency: p95 < 250ms for normal traffic (~up to 10k QPS peak for short bursts)
- Evidence: monthly telemetry export, 30 days retention of request traces for sampled requests, and a runbook for incident evidence collection

We need language that can sit as an exhibit to the MSA (SLO Rider) as well as any Order Form clarifications (e.g., billing credits, burst credits, and regional carve-outs). Legal would like an onboarding checklist so procurement can sign off fast.

Can you share your recommended exhibit and the onboarding checklist? Also confirm how you typically route these through DocuSign and what timelines we should expect. We attached preliminary internal requirements for context.

Jordan
Director, Platform Engineering
Mediq Health

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. We can do a tailored SLO Rider and an onboarding/acceptance checklist that maps to the Order Form. Quick outline of next steps and items we need from your side: 

1) Proposal: I attached our first-pass SLO Rider (RDW-SLO-Rider-Draft-v1.pdf) that includes availability language, latency tiers, and a proposed credit schedule. The Order Form annotations are called out inline for where we recommend explicit commitments.

2) Evidence & telemetry: to satisfy procurement we typically provide: daily aggregated SLO reports, monthly raw telemetry extract (CSV or S3 link), and an ops playbook for incident evidence collection. For your ask on traces, we can provide sampled request traces for 30 days for up to the routes specified in the Order Form. We need to confirm retention and any PII redact requirements.

3) Measurement method: our default measurement is regionally scoped API health checks and token-level request logs. If you require cross-region aggregation or different time-windowing for p95, please confirm.

4) Timing & signing: once we align on redlines, we route the SLO Rider and Order Form through DocuSign. Typical turnaround: 2–4 business days for signatures after legal signoff, assuming no further redlines.

Next actions: 
- Jordan: can your procurement/legal confirm the exact latency measurement window (p95 across which endpoints?) and any special audit requirements (e.g., third-party auditor reports beyond SOC2)?
- Kimberly & Marissa: I’m looping you to support redlines and confirm the DocuSign routing & billing adjustments.

I attached the draft SLO Rider and will wait for the Mediq redlines. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that speeds things up.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: Custom SLO rider + onboarding checklist (MSA & Order Form sign-off)

Diego / Marissa — quick legal review notes on the draft rider: 

- Measurement: replace “p95 measured globally” with “p95 measured per API route aggregated by region, with cross-region reporting available on request” — this prevents ambiguity on multi-region failover.
- Credits: recommend capping monthly credit exposure to a % of monthly committed spend and explicitly list the credit calculation formula. We should avoid an open-ended credit schedule.
- Evidence: accept monthly telemetry exports and incident packet exports for confirmed incidents, but limit trace retrieval to requests that are identifiable by a timestamp and request id (avoid broad mass extraction).
- Exceptions: add a carve-out for customer-driven testing (e.g., high-volume bulk imports initiated by Mediq), and for force majeure as per MSA.

Please get Karthik to review the billing/cost exposure side (capped credits) and Marissa to confirm DocuSign routing and whether we can use compressed telemetry exports (S3 link + manifest) as the standard.

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Diego / team — attached are Mediq's redlines (MediQ-procurement-redlines.docx). Key clarifications from procurement/legal: 

- Availability: confirm 99.95% monthly uptime for the set of production API endpoints listed in Appendix A of the Order Form.

- Availability: we will set the exhibit to 99.95% monthly for the endpoints in Appendix A and enumerate the exact endpoints in the SLO Rider.
- Latency: we will include p95 < 250ms for normal traffic on the primary endpoints and a graded credit band for surge windows > 60s.
